entries.creator: George Ripley (attributed); English alchemical tradition

entries.summary:
The Wellcome Ripley Scroll (WT 303, b18968831) is one of the finest surviving manuscript witnesses in the English alchemical scroll tradition attributed to George Ripley (c.1415–1490). The parchment roll is photographed here in 19 sections via the Wellcome Collection IIIF service.

## Iconography

Ripley Scrolls are vertical parchment rolls, typically 3–5 metres long, that narrate the alchemical Great Work through a sequence of emblematic images accompanied by Middle English verse stanzas. The standard iconographic program begins with a philosopher-alchemist bearing a staff and scroll, then proceeds through: the corrosion and dissolution stages (green lion devouring the sun; toad devouring the eagle); the philosophical conjunction of king (sol/sulphur) and queen (luna/mercury); alchemical vessels and the stages of the Work; and culminates with the crowned, triumphant Red King — the Philosopher's Stone in its final projection form. The verse texts interspersed between imagery are attributed to Ripley's *Compound of Alchymie* (1471) and allied poems.

Key iconographic symbols include: the **green lion** (vitriol/corrosive; dissolution of gold); the **eagle** (volatility/sublimation); the **toad** (fixation; the earth-bound principle); the **pelican** (multiplication; the pelican feeding her young with her blood is the *multiplicatio* stage); **Sol and Luna** (the royal pair, sulphur and mercury, joined in the philosophical marriage or *coniunctio*); the **nigredo dragon** (putrefaction; matter reduced to its prima materia); the **White Queen** (albedo; the purified silver stage); and the **Red King** (rubedo; the completed Stone).

## Significance

The Ripley Scroll tradition was enormously influential in English alchemy from c.1480 to c.1650, surviving in approximately 20–25 manuscript copies held at institutions including Princeton, the Huntington Library, the Getty, Yale, and the British Library. Jennifer Rampling's foundational study (*The Experimental Fire*, Chicago 2020) provides the most authoritative analysis of the scroll's textual tradition and its relationship to Ripley's other alchemical writings. Barbara Obrist (*Les Debuts de l'Imagerie Alchimique*) situates the scroll tradition within the broader medieval development of alchemical illustration. Lawrence Principe (*The Secrets of Alchemy*) provides the general scholarly context for English chrysopoeia.

The Wellcome WT 303 copy is held in the Wellcome Collection and is freely available via IIIF under their open access policy. It is one of the best-preserved colored copies of the scroll.

## For artists & game designers

The Ripley Scroll is a ready-made visual game structure: each painted panel is a stage or encounter, each symbol a game element. The 9-stage iconographic program maps cleanly to a progression system (corrosion → dissolution → conjunction → calcination → albedo → citrinitas → rubedo → multiplication → projection). The personified figures — green lion, white queen, red king — are direct character art templates. The vertical scroll format suggests game map design: a top-to-bottom level progression where the player descends or ascends through stages of transmutation.
